title: upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 + fused QKV/ROPE ops (kv-cache + continuous-batching + scheduler updates)
author: Evan Zhou
description: Context: We observed suboptimal throughput and higher p99 latency on long-context workloads due to non-optimal attention kernels and KV layout interactions with continuous batching and the request scheduler. This PR upgrades our attention kernels to a vetted FlashAttentionV2 implementation and introduces fused QKV + ROPE/rotary operations to reduce kernel launches and memory bandwidth. It also reworks the KV cache layout to be more compact and indexable for continuous batching, and updates the scheduler to do sequence-length-aware bin packing to form higher-quality batches. Changes in this PR: 1) Integrate FlashAttentionV2 kernels with a hardware-optimized codepath (CUDA/cuBLAS friendly); 2) Add fused QKV generation + rotary/ROPE application to reduce intermediate tensors and kernel round-trips; 3) New KV cache layout (contiguous per-request segments with pointer table) to speed up KV gather and reduce memory copies for continuous batching scenarios; 4) Scheduler improvements: sequence-length-aware binning and per-model kernel selection policy (prefer flashattnv2 when seq_len >= 512 or when quantization profile enables it); 5) Runtime feature flags and compatibility shim so older pinned model variants still use legacy kernels until rollout is validated; 6) Extensive perf harness and microbenchmarks, plus integration tests to guard correctness and determinism. Motivation: This work targets three production pain points: (a) reduce per-token cost by improving throughput on long context generations, (b) reduce tail latency by lowering kernel launch overhead and memory traffic, (c) make continuous batching more effective across heterogeneous request lengths. Benchmarks (representative): - A100 80GB, LLaMA-like model, seq_len 2048: 1.35x aggregated throughput vs legacy kernels; p99 latency down ~15%. - RTX 6000: 1.15x throughput improvement on seq_len 1024 workloads. - Token-level CPU overhead for KV serializing down ~40% in continuous-batching tests. Note: benchmarks run with the new kernel-selector enabled; exact gains vary by model architecture and quantization profile. Compatibility & rollout: feature-flag gated default-off; gradual rollout via model policy: tests passed on internal canary fleet; fallback to legacy kernels supported at model/version level. No public API changes. Only internal runtime and model registry entries updated. Testing: unit tests for kernel numerics included; deterministic integration tests for KV cache and batching; perf harness additions with automated daily runs against perf-canary infra. Checklist: - [x] Kernel integration + build config - [x] KV cache layout + serialization - [x] Scheduler changes + unit tests - [x] Benchmarks added to perf harness - [x] Docs/rollout notes - [x] Verified fallbacks and feature flags

Evan: Added a unit test (tests/unit/attn_numerics_test.py) and a nightly perf check that validates relative error across 10 random seeds.
Liam: The new KV pointer table looks good — did you validate memory alignment for host pinned allocation? We saw an alignment issue in a previous PR.
Evan: Yes, KV allocator enforces 256B alignment for pinned buffers; added comments and asserts in kv_cache_impl.cc.
Sofia: Scheduler changes look promising; please ensure the bin-packing budget doesn't starve low-latency short requests.
Evan: Scheduler policy now preserves a low-latency lane and uses a max-delay-ms threshold to avoid starvation; added a unit test to validate that short requests are served within SLO.
perf_summary: KV serialization CPU time: -40% in continuous-batching microbench
release_notes: Runtime: upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV+ROPE ops; improves throughput on long-context workloads and reduces p99 latency.
Runtime: new compact KV cache layout to improve continuous-batching throughput and reduce memory copies.
Scheduler: sequence-length-aware bin packing and kernel preference policy to select optimal kernels per workload.
Compatibility: rollout gated by feature flag; fallback to legacy kernels supported per model/version.
notes: This PR required CUDA 12 minimum for certain FlashAttentionV2 intrinsics; build matrix updated accordingly.
We validated numerics against legacy kernels with randomized seeds and included unit tests; long-tail edge cases should be monitored post-rollout.
Follow-up work: extend fused ops to support quantized int8 paths and evaluate further kernel fusion opportunities (ENG-8602).
